entries.title: Nobel Prize in Literature: László Krasznahorkai
entries.summary: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to the Hungarian novelist László Krasznahorkai (born 1954) "for his compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art." He is the second Hungarian Nobel laureate in Literature after Imre Kertész in 2002.

entries.title: Nobel Prize in Literature: Anne Carson
entries.summary: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian poet Anne Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature."
body: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian poet Anne Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature."

The Swedish Academy announced the decision in Stockholm on 8 October 2026, and the prize will be presented on 10 December. Established under the will of Alfred Nobel, the prize honors outstanding literary work.

provenance.full_source_extract:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian poet Anne Carson "for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature." 
The Swedish Academy announced the decision in Stockholm on 8 October 2026, and the prize will be presented on 10 December. Established under the will of Alfred Nobel, the prize honors outstanding literary work.
